newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka to boost winter charters from UK - paper.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka to boost winter charters from UK - paper.

text.p: Sri Lanka is to increase the number of charter flights operating out of Britain in the winter 1997 season, the independent Island newspaper said on Friday.
"The new charter operator approved by the president, British Caledonian, is expected to commence operations on November 1," the paper said.
Monarch Airways, which will also operate from the UK in the winter, was approved in March.

"Since Sri Lanka already has three year-round charter operators - Air Holland, Air Europe from Italy and Balair from Switzerland, the two new winter ones are very welcome," said Jagath Fernando, a director of John Keells Holdings Ltd, Sri Lanka's largest inbound tour operator.
Laudair from Austria is also a winter tour operator.
Sri Lanka's tourist industry is seen recovering from setbacks suffered last year when Tamil separatists bombed the Central Bank and a crowded passenger train, analysts said.

Tourist arrivals were up sharply by 20 percent in the first four months of 1997 over the same period last year, and the paper said Sri Lanka was looking at upward of 400,000 tourists arriving this year.
"We needed more charters to consolidate the revival and this is good news indeed," Fernando said.
The newspaper said British Airways and the national carrier Airlanka, which operate four and two flights each between Colombo and London every week, were unhappy about the latest charter operator.
The two British Airways and Airlanka object to charter flights as they offer heavily discounted tickets, the paper said.
Officials from both airlines were not immediately available for comment.
